questions.question_en: According to VSEPR theory, the shapes of ClF3, XeF4, and SF4 molecules are, respectively:
questions.question_hi:
[VSEPR & Molecular Geometry • IIT JAM Chemistry (CY) • Feb 2024]
According to VSEPR theory, the shapes of ClF3, XeF4, and SF4 molecules are, respectively:
options_en: Bent T-shaped, Square planar, and See-saw
Bent T-shaped, See-saw, and Square planar
options_hi: Bent T-shaped, Square planar, and See-saw
Bent T-shaped, See-saw, and Square planar
questions.explanation_en: ClF3 (AX3E2, 3 bond pairs + 2 lone pairs) is bent T-shaped; XeF4 (AX4E2, 4 bond pairs + 2 trans lone pairs) is square planar; SF4 (AX4E, 4 bond pairs + 1 equatorial lone pair) is see-saw.
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (IIT JAM Chemistry (CY) • Feb 2024):
ClF3 (AX3E2, 3 bond pairs + 2 lone pairs) is bent T-shaped; XeF4 (AX4E2, 4 bond pairs + 2 trans lone pairs) is square planar; SF4 (AX4E, 4 bond pairs + 1 equatorial lone pair) is see-saw.

questions.question_en: Upon one-electron ionization of O2 to form O2⁺ and of N2 to form N2⁺, how do their bond lengths change?
questions.question_hi:
[Molecular Orbital Theory (Diatomics) • IIT JAM Chemistry (CY) • Feb 2024]
Upon one-electron ionization of O2 to form O2⁺ and of N2 to form N2⁺, how do their bond lengths change?
options_en: O–O bond length decreases in O2⁺, while N–N bond length increases in N2⁺
O–O bond length increases in O2⁺, while N–N bond length decreases in N2⁺
options_hi: O–O bond length decreases in O2⁺, while N–N bond length increases in N2⁺
O–O bond length increases in O2⁺, while N–N bond length decreases in N2⁺
questions.explanation_en: In O2, an electron is removed from an antibonding π* orbital, increasing bond order from 2.0 to 2.5 and shortening the bond. In N2, an electron is removed from a bonding σ_{2p} orbital, decreasing bond order from 3.0 to 2.5 and lengthening the bond.
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (IIT JAM Chemistry (CY) • Feb 2024):
In O2, an electron is removed from an antibonding π* orbital, increasing bond order from 2.0 to 2.5 and shortening the bond. In N2, an electron is removed from a bonding σ_{2p} orbital, decreasing bond order from 3.0 to 2.5 and lengthening the bond.

questions.question_en: Among the following cyclic species — (I) Cyclopropenyl cation (C3H3⁺), (II) Cyclopentadienyl anion (C5H5⁻), (III) Tropylium cation (C7H7⁺), and (IV) Cyclooctatetraene (C8H8) — which are aromatic?

questions.explanation_en: C3H3⁺ (2 πe⁻, n=0), C5H5⁻ (6 πe⁻, n=1), and C7H7⁺ (6 πe⁻, n=1) are planar, cyclic, fully conjugated (4n+2) π-electron aromatic systems. C8H8 (8 πe⁻) adopts a non-planar tub conformation to avoid antiaromaticity.
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (IIT JAM Chemistry (CY) • Feb 2024):
C3H3⁺ (2 πe⁻, n=0), C5H5⁻ (6 πe⁻, n=1), and C7H7⁺ (6 πe⁻, n=1) are planar, cyclic, fully conjugated (4n+2) π-electron aromatic systems. C8H8 (8 πe⁻) adopts a non-planar tub conformation to avoid antiaromaticity.

questions.question_en: For an elementary chemical reaction, a plot of ln(k) versus 1/T yields a straight line with a negative slope equal to −6000 K. The activation energy E_a of the reaction (in kJ mol⁻¹, given R = 8.314 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹) is approximately:
questions.question_hi:
[Chemical Kinetics (Arrhenius Equation) • IIT JAM Chemistry (CY) • Feb 2024]

questions.explanation_en: From ln(k) = ln(A) − (E_a / R)(1/T), the slope is −E_a / R = −6000 K => E_a = 6000 K × 8.314 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ = 49,884 J mol⁻¹ ≈ 49.9 kJ mol⁻¹.
questions.explanation_hi:

From ln(k) = ln(A) − (E_a / R)(1/T), the slope is −E_a / R = −6000 K => E_a = 6000 K × 8.314 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ = 49,884 J mol⁻¹ ≈ 49.9 kJ mol⁻¹.

questions.question_en: Using Crystal Field Stabilization Energy (CFSE) preferences for octahedral vs tetrahedral sites, the structures of Fe3O4 (magnetite) and Mn3O4 (hausmannite) are, respectively:
questions.question_hi:
[Coordination Chemistry (Spinel Structure) • IIT JAM Chemistry (CY) • Feb 2024]
Using Crystal Field Stabilization Energy (CFSE) preferences for octahedral vs tetrahedral sites, the structures of Fe3O4 (magnetite) and Mn3O4 (hausmannite) are, respectively:
questions.explanation_en: In Fe3O4 (Fe²⁺Fe³⁺₂O4), high-spin Fe³⁺ (d⁵) has zero CFSE in both sites whereas Fe²⁺ (d⁶) has higher octahedral CFSE (−0.4 Δ_o vs −0.6 Δ_t), giving an inverse spinel. In Mn3O4 (Mn²⁺Mn³⁺₂O4), Mn³⁺ (d⁴) has strong octahedral CFSE while Mn²⁺ (d⁵) has zero CFSE, giving a normal spinel.
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (IIT JAM Chemistry (CY) • Feb 2024):
In Fe3O4 (Fe²⁺Fe³⁺₂O4), high-spin Fe³⁺ (d⁵) has zero CFSE in both sites whereas Fe²⁺ (d⁶) has higher octahedral CFSE (−0.4 Δ_o vs −0.6 Δ_t), giving an inverse spinel. In Mn3O4 (Mn²⁺Mn³⁺₂O4), Mn³⁺ (d⁴) has strong octahedral CFSE while Mn²⁺ (d⁵) has zero CFSE, giving a normal spinel.

questions.question_en: According to the Woodward-Hoffmann conservation of orbital symmetry rules, the thermal ring opening of cis-3,4-dimethylcyclobutene proceeds via a:

questions.question_en: Consider the concentration cell at 298 K: Ag(s) | AgNO3 (0.01 M) || AgNO3 (1.0 M) | Ag(s). Assuming complete dissociation and unit activity coefficients (with 2.303 RT / F = 0.059 V), the cell EMF E_cell is:

questions.explanation_en: For a 1-electron concentration cell (n = 1), E_cell = (0.059 V / 1) log10([Ag⁺]_cathode / [Ag⁺]_anode) = 0.059 × log10(1.0 / 0.01) = 0.059 × 2 = +0.118 V.

For a 1-electron concentration cell (n = 1), E_cell = (0.059 V / 1) log10([Ag⁺]_cathode / [Ag⁺]_anode) = 0.059 × log10(1.0 / 0.01) = 0.059 × 2 = +0.118 V.

questions.question_en: For the acidic amino acid L-aspartic acid with pK_a1 (α-COOH) = 2.0, pK_a2 (side-chain β-COOH) = 3.9, and pK_a3 (α-NH3⁺) = 9.9, the isoelectric point (pI) is:

[Bioorganic Chemistry (Amino Acids & Isoelectric Point) • IIT JAM Chemistry (CY) • Feb 2024]

questions.explanation_en: For an acidic amino acid, the neutral zwitterion lies between the two carboxyl deprotonations pK_a1 and pK_a2, so pI = (pK_a1 + pK_a2) / 2 = (2.0 + 3.9) / 2 = 2.95.

questions.question_en: Given the kinetic trans-directing series in square-planar Pt(II) substitutions: Cl⁻ < NH3 ? Wait: the true trans-effect order is NH3 < Cl⁻ < Br⁻ < NO2⁻ < CN⁻ ≈ C2H4 ≈ CO. Starting from [PtCl4]²⁻ and treating sequentially with (1) NH3 (1 equiv.) and (2) NO2⁻ (1 equiv.), the stereoisomer formed is:
questions.question_hi:
[Inorganic Chemistry (Trans Effect in Pt(II) Complexes) • IIT JAM Chemistry (CY) • Feb 2024]
Given the kinetic trans-directing series in square-planar Pt(II) substitutions: Cl⁻ < NH3 ? Wait: the true trans-effect order is NH3 < Cl⁻ < Br⁻ < NO2⁻ < CN⁻ ≈ C2H4 ≈ CO. Starting from [PtCl4]²⁻ and treating sequentially with (1) NH3 (1 equiv.) and (2) NO2⁻ (1 equiv.), the stereoisomer formed is:
questions.explanation_en: First, 1 equiv. of NH3 substitutes one Cl⁻ of [PtCl4]²⁻ to give [PtCl3(NH3)]⁻. Since the trans effect of Cl⁻ is greater than that of NH3 (Cl⁻ > NH3), the incoming NO2⁻ substitutes one of the two Cl⁻ ligands that are mutually trans to each other (and cis to NH3), giving cis-[PtCl2(NH3)(NO2)]⁻.
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (IIT JAM Chemistry (CY) • Feb 2024):
First, 1 equiv. of NH3 substitutes one Cl⁻ of [PtCl4]²⁻ to give [PtCl3(NH3)]⁻. Since the trans effect of Cl⁻ is greater than that of NH3 (Cl⁻ > NH3), the incoming NO2⁻ substitutes one of the two Cl⁻ ligands that are mutually trans to each other (and cis to NH3), giving cis-[PtCl2(NH3)(NO2)]⁻.

questions.question_en: Which of the following statement(s) about trivalent lanthanide ions (Ln³⁺) is/are TRUE?
questions.question_hi:
[Lanthanide Chemistry & Magnetic Moments • IIT JAM Chemistry (CY) • Feb 2024]
Which of the following statement(s) about trivalent lanthanide ions (Ln³⁺) is/are TRUE?
options_en: Their 4f orbitals are deeply buried and shielded by 5s²5p⁶ electrons, resulting in very weak crystal field splitting and sharp f–f absorption bands.
The magnetic moments of most Ln³⁺ ions must be calculated using the spin-orbit coupled formula μ_eff = g_J √[J(J+1)] μ_B rather than the spin-only formula.
Across the series from La³⁺ to Lu³⁺, the ionic radius decreases steadily (Lanthanide Contraction), causing Zr and Hf to have nearly identical atomic/ionic radii.
Ce⁴⁺ is a strong reducing agent in aqueous solution.
options_hi: Their 4f orbitals are deeply buried and shielded by 5s²5p⁶ electrons, resulting in very weak crystal field splitting and sharp f–f absorption bands.
The magnetic moments of most Ln³⁺ ions must be calculated using the spin-orbit coupled formula μ_eff = g_J √[J(J+1)] μ_B rather than the spin-only formula.
Across the series from La³⁺ to Lu³⁺, the ionic radius decreases steadily (Lanthanide Contraction), causing Zr and Hf to have nearly identical atomic/ionic radii.
Ce⁴⁺ is a strong reducing agent in aqueous solution.
questions.explanation_en: 4f orbitals are core-like, giving sharp atomic-like f–f bands and strong spin-orbit coupling (so J is a good quantum number). Lanthanide contraction makes 4d (Zr) and 5d (Hf) radii nearly identical. Note that Ce⁴⁺ (4f⁰) is a strong oxidizing agent, not reducing agent.
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (IIT JAM Chemistry (CY) • Feb 2024):
4f orbitals are core-like, giving sharp atomic-like f–f bands and strong spin-orbit coupling (so J is a good quantum number). Lanthanide contraction makes 4d (Zr) and 5d (Hf) radii nearly identical. Note that Ce⁴⁺ (4f⁰) is a strong oxidizing agent, not reducing agent.

questions.question_en: For the orbitals of a Hydrogen atom, which of the following statement(s) is/are CORRECT?
questions.question_hi:
[Quantum Chemistry (Hydrogenic Wavefunctions) • IIT JAM Chemistry (CY) • Feb 2024]
For the orbitals of a Hydrogen atom, which of the following statement(s) is/are CORRECT?
options_en: A 3p orbital has 1 radial node and 1 angular (planar) node.
A 3d_{z²} orbital has 0 radial nodes and 2 conical angular nodes.
The radial probability distribution P(r) = 4π r² |R_{nl}(r)|² for the 1s orbital has its maximum at the Bohr radius r = a0.
All orbitals with the same angular momentum quantum number l are degenerate in a multi-electron atom.
options_hi: A 3p orbital has 1 radial node and 1 angular (planar) node.
A 3d_{z²} orbital has 0 radial nodes and 2 conical angular nodes.
The radial probability distribution P(r) = 4π r² |R_{nl}(r)|² for the 1s orbital has its maximum at the Bohr radius r = a0.
All orbitals with the same angular momentum quantum number l are degenerate in a multi-electron atom.
questions.explanation_en: Radial nodes = n − l − 1 (1 for 3p, 0 for 3d) and angular nodes = l (1 for 3p, 2 for 3d). For 1s, P(r) ∝ r² e^(−2r/a0) peaks at dP/dr = 0 => r = a0.
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (IIT JAM Chemistry (CY) • Feb 2024):
Radial nodes = n − l − 1 (1 for 3p, 0 for 3d) and angular nodes = l (1 for 3p, 2 for 3d). For 1s, P(r) ∝ r² e^(−2r/a0) peaks at dP/dr = 0 => r = a0.

questions.question_en: Which of the following statement(s) regarding ideal dilute solutions of non-volatile solutes is/are TRUE?

questions.question_en: The spin-only magnetic moment (in Bohr Magnetons, BM, rounded to two decimal places) of the tetrahedral complex [CoCl4]²⁻ is ________.
questions.question_hi:
[Coordination Chemistry (Spin-Only Magnetic Moment) • IIT JAM Chemistry (CY) • Feb 2024]
The spin-only magnetic moment (in Bohr Magnetons, BM, rounded to two decimal places) of the tetrahedral complex [CoCl4]²⁻ is ________.
questions.explanation_en: In [CoCl4]²⁻, Co²⁺ is a 3d⁷ ion in a tetrahedral field (e⁴ t2³) with n = 3 unpaired electrons. Thus μ_so = √[n(n+2)] = √[3(5)] = √15 ≈ 3.87 BM.
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (IIT JAM Chemistry (CY) • Feb 2024):
In [CoCl4]²⁻, Co²⁺ is a 3d⁷ ion in a tetrahedral field (e⁴ t2³) with n = 3 unpaired electrons. Thus μ_so = √[n(n+2)] = √[3(5)] = √15 ≈ 3.87 BM.

questions.question_en: The Index of Hydrogen Deficiency (Degree of Unsaturation) of the aromatic hydrocarbon naphthalene (C10H8) is ________.
questions.question_hi:
[Organic Chemistry (Degree of Unsaturation / IHD) • IIT JAM Chemistry (CY) • Feb 2024]
The Index of Hydrogen Deficiency (Degree of Unsaturation) of the aromatic hydrocarbon naphthalene (C10H8) is ________.
questions.explanation_en: IHD = C − H/2 + N/2 + 1 = 10 − 8/2 + 0 + 1 = 7 (2 fused rings + 5 π bonds = 7).
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (IIT JAM Chemistry (CY) • Feb 2024):
IHD = C − H/2 + N/2 + 1 = 10 − 8/2 + 0 + 1 = 7 (2 fused rings + 5 π bonds = 7).

questions.question_en: First-order (n = 1) Bragg diffraction of X-rays of wavelength λ = 1.54 Å from the (111) planes of a cubic crystal occurs at a glancing angle θ = 30°. The interplanar spacing d_{111} (in Å, rounded to two decimal places) is ________.
questions.question_hi:
[Solid State Chemistry (Bragg's Law) • IIT JAM Chemistry (CY) • Feb 2024]
First-order (n = 1) Bragg diffraction of X-rays of wavelength λ = 1.54 Å from the (111) planes of a cubic crystal occurs at a glancing angle θ = 30°. The interplanar spacing d_{111} (in Å, rounded to two decimal places) is ________.
questions.explanation_en: By Bragg's Law, 2 d sin(θ) = n λ. Since sin(30°) = 0.5 and n = 1, d = λ / (2 × 0.5) = λ = 1.54 Å.
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (IIT JAM Chemistry (CY) • Feb 2024):
By Bragg's Law, 2 d sin(θ) = n λ. Since sin(30°) = 0.5 and n = 1, d = λ / (2 × 0.5) = λ = 1.54 Å.

questions.question_en: Using the Henderson-Hasselbalch equation, the pH of an aqueous buffer solution containing 0.20 M acetic acid (pK_a = 4.76) and 0.20 M sodium acetate at 298 K is ________.
questions.question_hi:
[Ionic Equilibrium (pH of Weak Acid Buffer) • IIT JAM Chemistry (CY) • Feb 2024]
Using the Henderson-Hasselbalch equation, the pH of an aqueous buffer solution containing 0.20 M acetic acid (pK_a = 4.76) and 0.20 M sodium acetate at 298 K is ________.
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (IIT JAM Chemistry (CY) • Feb 2024):
pH = pK_a + log10([Salt]/[Acid]) = 4.76 + log10(0.20 / 0.20) = 4.76.

questions.question_en: A radioactive isotope undergoes first-order decay with a half-life t_{1/2} = 15 minutes. The time (in minutes) required for 87.5% of the initial sample to decay (leaving 12.5% unreacted) is ________.
questions.question_hi:
[Chemical Kinetics (First-Order Half-Life) • IIT JAM Chemistry (CY) • Feb 2024]
A radioactive isotope undergoes first-order decay with a half-life t_{1/2} = 15 minutes. The time (in minutes) required for 87.5% of the initial sample to decay (leaving 12.5% unreacted) is ________.
questions.explanation_en: Leaving 12.5% = 1/8 = (1/2)³ of the initial sample requires exactly 3 half-lives: t = 3 × 15 min = 45 minutes.
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (IIT JAM Chemistry (CY) • Feb 2024):
Leaving 12.5% = 1/8 = (1/2)³ of the initial sample requires exactly 3 half-lives: t = 3 × 15 min = 45 minutes.

questions.question_en: A reversible Carnot heat engine operates between a hot reservoir at 600 K and a cold sink at 300 K. If the engine absorbs 120 kJ of heat from the hot reservoir per cycle, the maximum work output W (in kJ) per cycle is ________.
questions.question_hi:
[Thermodynamics (Carnot Engine Efficiency) • IIT JAM Chemistry (CY) • Feb 2024]
A reversible Carnot heat engine operates between a hot reservoir at 600 K and a cold sink at 300 K. If the engine absorbs 120 kJ of heat from the hot reservoir per cycle, the maximum work output W (in kJ) per cycle is ________.
questions.explanation_en: Carnot efficiency η = 1 − T_C / T_H = 1 − 300 / 600 = 0.50. Thus W = η Q_H = 0.50 × 120 kJ = 60 kJ.
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (IIT JAM Chemistry (CY) • Feb 2024):
Carnot efficiency η = 1 − T_C / T_H = 1 − 300 / 600 = 0.50. Thus W = η Q_H = 0.50 × 120 kJ = 60 kJ.

questions.question_en: Pure (S)-(+)-2-butanol has a specific rotation [α]_D = +13.5°. A non-racemic sample of 2-butanol containing 80% of the (S)-(+) enantiomer and 20% of the (R)-(−) enantiomer has an observed specific rotation (in degrees, rounded to one decimal place) of ________.
questions.question_hi:
[Stereochemistry (Enantiomeric Excess & Specific Rotation) • IIT JAM Chemistry (CY) • Feb 2024]
Pure (S)-(+)-2-butanol has a specific rotation [α]_D = +13.5°. A non-racemic sample of 2-butanol containing 80% of the (S)-(+) enantiomer and 20% of the (R)-(−) enantiomer has an observed specific rotation (in degrees, rounded to one decimal place) of ________.
questions.explanation_en: Enantiomeric excess ee = 80% − 20% = 60% = 0.60. Observed specific rotation = 0.60 × (+13.5°) = +8.1°.
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (IIT JAM Chemistry (CY) • Feb 2024):
Enantiomeric excess ee = 80% − 20% = 60% = 0.60. Observed specific rotation = 0.60 × (+13.5°) = +8.1°.

questions.question_en: An aqueous solution of a transition-metal complex with molar absorptivity ε = 4000 L mol⁻¹ cm⁻¹ shows an absorbance A = 0.80 in a cuvette of path length l = 1.0 cm. The molar concentration of the complex (in mmol L⁻¹) is ________.
questions.question_hi:
[Bioinorganic & Analytical Chemistry (Lambert-Beer Law) • IIT JAM Chemistry (CY) • Feb 2024]
An aqueous solution of a transition-metal complex with molar absorptivity ε = 4000 L mol⁻¹ cm⁻¹ shows an absorbance A = 0.80 in a cuvette of path length l = 1.0 cm. The molar concentration of the complex (in mmol L⁻¹) is ________.
questions.explanation_en: By the Beer-Lambert Law, c = A / (ε l) = 0.80 / (4000 × 1.0) = 2.0 × 10⁻⁴ mol L⁻¹ = 0.20 mmol L⁻¹.
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (IIT JAM Chemistry (CY) • Feb 2024):
By the Beer-Lambert Law, c = A / (ε l) = 0.80 / (4000 × 1.0) = 2.0 × 10⁻⁴ mol L⁻¹ = 0.20 mmol L⁻¹.

questions.question_en: In the dirhenium octachloride dianion [Re2Cl8]²⁻ (with eclipsed D_{4h} geometry and Re(III) 5d⁴ centers), the formal Re–Re bond order is ________.
questions.question_hi:
[Organometallics (Metal-Metal Bond Order in Re2Cl8²⁻) • IIT JAM Chemistry (CY) • Feb 2024]
In the dirhenium octachloride dianion [Re2Cl8]²⁻ (with eclipsed D_{4h} geometry and Re(III) 5d⁴ centers), the formal Re–Re bond order is ________.
questions.explanation_en: Each Re(III) is 5d⁴, contributing 8 d-electrons to the metal-metal manifold in the configuration σ² π⁴ δ² δ*⁰, giving a quadruple (bond order = 4) Re–Re bond.
questions.explanation_hi:
